claims.text: TiVNbTa is a refractory high-entropy alloy with high-temperature strength and room-temperature ductility.
Conventionally synthesized TiVNbTa contains trace interstitial oxygen and nitrogen.
Vacuum melting and controlled inert-atmosphere processing will minimize oxygen and nitrogen incorporation.
Reducing oxygen and nitrogen will prevent impurity-induced phase segregation in the alloy.
Reducing oxygen and nitrogen will enhance high-temperature strength.
The purification intervention will preserve the alloy's low density.
The purification intervention will preserve good room-temperature ductility.
The intervention will be effective from approximately 700°C to 1100°C under mechanical loading.
Lower impurity levels will produce a more homogeneous microstructure with reduced susceptibility to phase segregation.
Trace oxygen and nitrogen promote phase segregation during thermal aging of TiVNbTa.
Phase segregation depletes strengthening interstitial solutes from the metal matrix.
Depletion of interstitial solutes from the matrix causes progressive age softening.
Lowering the initial interstitial content will preserve high-temperature solid-solution strengthening.
The purified alloy will have significantly higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the conventionally processed baseline.
The purified alloy will exhibit less age softening than the conventionally processed baseline.
The targeted high-temperature strength improvement is above 800–1000 MPa relative to the baseline.
The purified alloy will retain comparable room-temperature mechanical performance and density.
Conventionally processed TiVNbTa undergoes age softening during high-temperature aging.
A critical oxygen and nitrogen concentration exists below which the proposed improvement occurs.
The optimal impurity threshold and exact strength improvement remain unknown.

contradictions.description: The intervention seeks to minimize oxygen and nitrogen, while the mechanism acknowledges that these interstitials provide solid-solution strengthening and claims their strengthening will be preserved. No residual concentration or processing route is specified that would suppress segregation while retaining enough interstitial solute for strengthening.
